the design and fabrication of porous nanorod bifunctional cathode material with a spinel structure.
the development of a novel bifunctional cathode material, FeCo2O3, for Li-O2 batteries.
the design of a new type of spinel MCo(2)O(4) (M = Mn(2+), Co(2+), Zn(2+), or Ni(2+)) nanorods, which are used as bifunctional cathode materials for Li-O(2) batteries.

FeCo2O3 nanorods have the best electrochemical performance as bifunctional cathode material for Li-O2 battery applications.
the porous FeCo 2 O 4 nanorods are the most promising cathode for Li-O 2 batteries.
the substitution on the A site with Fe(2+) can effectively enhance the electrocatalytic activity and cycling performance of the spinel MCo(2)O4 cathode in the Li-O2 battery system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FeCo2 O4 porous nanorods can be a promising bifunctional electrocatalyst in Li-O2 batteries.
the FeCo2 oxide has the highest Co ratio and the highest oxygen adsorption energy, which can facilitate the oxygen reduction reaction and oxygen evolution reaction.
the porous nanorod structured MCo2O2 (M = Mn(2+), Zn(2+), Mn(2+)Fe(2+), Co(2+), Cu(2+)) are promising cathode electrocatalysts for Li-O2 batteries, especially the FeCo2 O4 nanorods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spinel MCoO2 (M = Mn(2+), Co(2+), Zn(2+), or Ni(2+)) cathode can be a potential candidate for the development of a high-performance nonaqueous rechargeable Li-O2 battery.
the spinel structure can be used to develop high-performance bifunctional catalysts for the Li-O2 battery, and the FeCo2 oxide is the most promising cathode for Li-O2 battery application.
